long_context._comment: A RAG-sized turn (SPEC §8.3 returns top-5 reranked chunks, i.e. thousands of tokens of manual text). Prefill dominates here, and on Marlin that is where the quantization cost lands, so this is the number that says whether a cited answer from M4 can be read aloud without an awkward pause. Measured at ~10,100 prompt tokens on 2026-09-25 — the character-based estimate that sized this text said ~6,000, which is why the run records the server's own prompt_tokens rather than trusting an estimate. At 10k it is a pessimistic RAG turn rather than a typical one (top-5 chunks of 400-700 tokens plus the system prompt and tool schemas is nearer 4-5k), and it is left at this size deliberately: the number worth knowing is the one that does not flatter. EVERY STREAM GETS ITS OWN CONTEXT. `contexts[0]` is the single stream and `contexts[1..]` the concurrent ones; they differ from their first line, so no stream can reuse a prefix another just cached. Sharing one context measured the prefix cache instead of load, and made the concurrent figures look faster than the single one (see docs/MODEL_EVAL.md, 2026-09-25). Recipe: 137 lines of 'machine — section — punkt N' with a seeded random.Random(index) drawing from a per-index machine pool; punkt 1..137 exist in each, so the same question is answerable against all of them. Synthetic: every machine, part number and figure here is invented.
